cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: Stensul Brings Governed Creation to Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next
stories.plain: Stensul's new beta integration lets marketers and AI agents build and personalize campaigns inside Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next, then push them straight to activation. This matters because it embeds governance guardrails directly into the AI-assisted creation workflow, meaning content made by agents must pass approval rules before it reaches customers — a model other platforms will likely copy.

stories.head: Vibe Expands Connected TV Platform With Agent Access and Six New Integrations
stories.plain: Advertisers can now launch and manage streaming TV campaigns by talking to Claude or ChatGPT, or via API from their own tools. This is a significant shift: AI agents can now buy and manage CTV media autonomously, which changes how performance marketers think about campaign execution and removes the need to log into a dedicated ad interface.

stories.head: Martech Portfolio Intelligence: Using AI to Decide Which Marketing Technologies Deserve to Survive
stories.plain: A practical framework for using AI to audit and rationalise a bloated martech stack — covering CDPs, automation, analytics, personalization and more. This matters for buyers and budget holders because AI-driven portfolio audits are becoming a standard governance practice, directly affecting which vendors get renewed and which get cut in the next planning cycle.

stories.head: AI Search Is Rewriting Brand Visibility — Earned Media Is Becoming Infrastructure
stories.plain: The piece argues that as AI answers replace search result pages, the question shifts from ranking to whether AI models judge your brand credible enough to cite. Earned media — press, reviews, citations — is now the raw material that feeds generative engine visibility, making PR and content strategy a direct input to AI discoverability budgets.

stories.head: DoubleVerify Launches Ask Neura, a Conversational AI Layer Across Media Intelligence
stories.plain: DoubleVerify has built a natural-language interface directly into its DV Pinnacle platform, letting advertisers and agencies query media quality data and get actionable recommendations across social, CTV, and open web — without digging through dashboards. Conversational access to verification data lowers the skill barrier for media governance and could accelerate how quickly teams act on brand-safety signals.

stories.head: HubSpot rebuilds its platform around AI agents
stories.plain: HubSpot's redesigned Breeze Assistant coordinates a layer of AI agents while a continuously self-updating CRM supplies the business context they need to act. This is a core architectural shift — not a feature add — that changes how a dominant mid-market CRM platform is bought and integrated, setting a new baseline expectation for agentic CRM.

stories.head: Does anyone understand the CDP market anymore?
stories.plain: BlueConic's CEO explains how AI agents and M&A have fundamentally reshaped the CDP category over three years, blurring its boundaries with CEPs and data warehouses. Essential orientation for anyone buying or building on a CDP today — the market you thought you understood no longer exists in the same form.

stories.head: The problem with AI doing exactly what you ask
stories.plain: A sharp governance piece arguing that poorly specified objectives — not rogue behaviour — are the real AI risk. Agents can optimize relentlessly toward a wrong goal and cause serious damage without ever going off-script. Directly relevant to anyone deploying agentic decisioning in marketing workflows.

stories.head: Salesforce bets CRM experience can give its AI an edge
stories.plain: Salesforce's new Koa reasoning model is trained on decades of CRM operational data to handle the behind-the-scenes work of customer interactions. This matters because proprietary training data — not just model size — is becoming the competitive moat in enterprise marketing AI, shaping which platforms win long-term deals.

stories.head: AI Search Is Rewriting Brand Visibility. Earned Media Is Becoming Infrastructure.
stories.plain: The piece reframes the question from ranking in search to being recognised as credible enough for AI to cite. As generative engines replace traditional SERPs for discovery, earned media coverage and third-party validation become the new technical infrastructure for brand visibility — a direct budget and strategy implication.

themes.head: Platforms rebuild around agents, not features
body: HubSpot, Salesforce, LeanData, and MoEngage all made major moves this month to restructure their core platforms so that AI agents are the primary unit of execution, not dashboards or workflows. This is not an add-on layer — it signals that the underlying architecture of MarTech is being rewritten from the ground up.

The governance question is emerging fast: once agents launch, who owns their decisions and their drift? The industry has no settled answer yet, and that ambiguity creates real risk for marketing teams that deploy agents without clear accountability frameworks in place.

themes.head: AI search makes earned media infrastructure
body: As AI-powered search surfaces answers instead of blue links, brand visibility is now determined by what gets cited, not what gets clicked. Earned media — press, reviews, expert mentions — is shifting from a PR metric to a foundational distribution layer that feeds the models deciding what audiences see.

This forces a strategic reframe: content and reputation programs that once lived in comms budgets must now be treated as core search infrastructure. The brand guidelines problem compounds this — AI exposes every gap in tone and positioning that humans used to paper over manually.

themes.head: Measuring AI against the wrong goal
body: A recurring signal this month is that most organizations are benchmarking AI tools on efficiency and output volume — the wrong scorecard. The more consequential question is whether AI is changing outcomes: revenue, retention, decision quality — and that requires a different measurement architecture entirely.

Related warnings surfaced around AI doing exactly what you asked but not what you meant, and around unsafe automation in live ad accounts. The pattern is consistent: deployment is outpacing the governance and measurement frameworks needed to make it safe and strategic.

themes.head: Stack rationalization as portfolio intelligence
body: The conversation around MarTech consolidation has matured: it is no longer just about cutting tools, but about using AI itself to audit which platforms earn their place in the stack. Portfolio intelligence — systematic, data-driven evaluation of technology ROI — is becoming its own discipline.

The CDP market confusion flagged this month reflects the same pressure from the opposite direction: category boundaries are dissolving as platforms absorb adjacent capabilities. Teams that cannot articulate what each tool uniquely delivers will find AI-driven audits making the decision for them.

themes.head: Connected TV & retail media reach full-funnel maturity
body: DoorDash's framing of retail media as awareness-to-doorstep in 30 minutes, combined with Vibe's CTV platform adding agent access and six new integrations, marks a turning point: performance and brand channels are converging into a single measurable loop. CTV is no longer a reach-only vehicle — it is a full-funnel instrument with commerce attached.

IAB Tech Lab's proposed new programmatic rules and Viamedia.ai's local-first omnichannel OS signal that the infrastructure layer is catching up to the ambition. Advertisers who treat CTV and retail media as separate line items will increasingly be at a structural disadvantage against those running them as one integrated system.

month.takeaway: Every major move this month points to the same pressure: AI is forcing marketing organizations to rebuild their platforms, measurement, governance, and channel strategies simultaneously — and most are only ready for one at a time.
